title: Rookie Drill on Wet Asphalt
premise: A long firefighter drama under orange-red helmets and wet-asphalt glare. Zhuqing and A-Qiao are easily confused; the positive-pressure respirator goes airtight→mask-cracked→replaced-repaired; fire engine Ladder One is wrecked and must be avoided; count memory, false friends, and temporal flashbacks run throughout. Human-readable context only; never fed to the SUT.

states.prime_trainer: Squad leader Huo Yan in his forties, buzz cut going gray, deep-blue drill uniform under an orange-red reflective vest, radio on the shoulder, old burn scar on the arm.
states.burned_with_crutch: The same Huo Yan after burns: fresh bandage on the neck, left-leg splint, walking slowly on a metal crutch, still in that soot-stained deep-blue drill uniform.
states.deceased: Huo Yan has closed his eyes in death, lying still on a narrow bed in the medic room, face peaceful, no breath left.

states.young_rookie: Young Zhuqing: a lean seventeen-year-old firefighter rookie, orange-red helmet, deep-blue drill uniform, cyan 'Qing' arm patch on the left arm, bright stubborn eyes.
states.adult_fighter: Adult Zhuqing: a tall upright firefighter around twenty-three or twenty-four, still in orange-red helmet with cyan 'Qing' arm patch on the left arm, calm bearing.

states.airtight: A backpack positive-pressure respirator, matte-black cylinder intact, facepiece clear unmarked, supply hose coiled neat.
states.mask_cracked: The same positive-pressure respirator with a cracked facepiece, supply hose half-detached, airtight alarm flashing red.
states.replaced_repaired: After a new facepiece and hose, the positive-pressure respirator is airtight again; a maintenance stamp on the cylinder marks it apart from the first intact state.

states.intact: A waterproof-cover training log, company number on the cover, pages packed with drill subjects and times in marker.
states.water_stained: The same training log soaked by a hose stream, cover warped, writing bled into blue blotches.

states.intact: A bright-red aerial fire engine, white 'Ladder One' sprayed on the door, telescopic ladder stowed on the roof, orange-yellow hose hung on the body.
states.rollover_wrecked: The bright-red fire engine rolled and wrecked, ladder bent, hoses scattered—a wreck that can no longer respond.

states.young_observer: Young A-Qiao: nearly identical in face to Zhuqing, but lemon-yellow helmet, silver rappel badge on the right arm, bolder expression.
states.adult_publicist: Adult A-Qiao: nearly identical in face to adult Zhuqing, still in lemon-yellow helmet with rappel badge, publicity camera on the shoulder.

segments.action: At dusk, Huo Yan pushes into the company training hall; a positive-pressure respirator stands on a rack at the floor center.
A row of five helmet lamps hangs on the east-wall charging rack; Huo Yan checks each battery.
In the drill-yard porch hang two assembly brass bells; Huo Yan reaches out and lets the tongues tap lightly.
Huo Yan circles the positive-pressure respirator, checking facepiece seal and cylinder valve.
Huo Yan looks out the window at the sky beyond the wet asphalt drill yard.
The intact positive-pressure respirator stands quietly at the center of the training hall.
Huo Yan sits on a long bench and dozes under the ceiling lights.
Night wind pours through the main door; Huo Yan zips his reflective vest tight.
Huo Yan opens the training log and records that night's rappel times.
Huo Yan draws a water-pressure curve in the training log.
Huo Yan closes the training log and returns it to the duty-desk drawer.
Cylinder-valve gleam from the positive-pressure respirator sweeps Huo Yan's profile.
Huo Yan gently wipes mist from the facepiece with a dry cloth.
On the morning wet asphalt drill yard, Huo Yan greets young Zhuqing driving bright-red Ladder One in.
Zhuqing jumps down from Ladder One and retightens the helmet chin strap.
Huo Yan points to three hose dividers by the hose rack, teaching Zhuqing to read caliber and couplings.
Zhuqing crouches on the wet asphalt, curiously touching the helmet outline in the reflection.
Huo Yan points at the drill tower, explaining high-rise evacuation routes to Zhuqing.
Zhuqing looks back at parked Ladder One, eyes full of longing.
The two lean side by side against the drill-tower base, listening to a distant alarm test.
In the gear-bay corridor, A-Qiao in a lemon-yellow helmet turns to look from behind air cylinders.

Huo Yan opens the training log and finds the cover soaked by a hose stream, writing bled into blue blotches.

segments.action: Seasons turn; day after day Huo Yan walks into the company training hall to train the squad.
Another snowy night, Huo Yan wraps his vest tight and keeps watch beside the positive-pressure respirator.
Spring camp opens; Huo Yan calibrates rappel anchors in the hall.
At midsummer noon, Huo Yan wipes drill-tower rails heated by the fierce sun.
Autumn rain stretches on; the positive-pressure respirator facepiece fogs in the damp.
Another New Year's Eve, Huo Yan keeps watch alone in the training hall until dawn.
The night before competition, Huo Yan checks hose couplings two hours early.
On a full-moon night, Huo Yan fully charges every helmet lamp.
A cold wave hits; Huo Yan hangs a windbreak curtain on the hall's main door.
Around Qingming, Huo Yan sweeps leaves and grit from the wet asphalt drill yard.
In plum-rain season, Huo Yan repeatedly checks air-cylinder valves for rust.
On the first frost of winter, white breath from Huo Yan drifts under a helmet lamp.
In antifreeze-drill week, Huo Yan drains residual water from the hoses clean.
On New Year duty, Huo Yan sorts hose-divider numbers by the duty desk.
Three quiet nights without alarms, Huo Yan rearranges the fitness schedule again and again.
One foggy night, Huo Yan has to shorten the outdoor high-rise class.
A false alarm sounds; Huo Yan quickly counts heads and clears it.
At three a.m., Huo Yan drinks cold tea from a thermos.
By the hose rack he sorts sealing rings for the hose dividers.
Assembly brass bells toll low in the wind; Huo Yan looks up and listens.
As the sky pales, Huo Yan records last night's final set of times.
Before lights-out he takes one last look at the airtight facepiece of the positive-pressure respirator.
After the rain stops, he sweeps standing water on the wet asphalt toward the drain.
At dawn, Huo Yan patrols the wet asphalt drill yard; bright-red Ladder One sits by the drill tower.
Huo Yan crouches to check Ladder One's tires and ladder lock pins.
Huo Yan walks to the hose rack; those three hose dividers are still lined up neat.
A strange gray-green troop truck passes the compound road—hose rolls in the bed, not Ladder One.
Huo Yan stands on the wet asphalt, logging last night's peak wind speed.
Huo Yan relays anti-slip mats at the drill-tower entrance.
Far morning fog lifts, revealing a deeper city skyline.
Flashover erupts; the company training hall shudders in the blast wave; the positive-pressure respirator shakes hard.
Heat washes over; Huo Yan rushes for the emergency shutoff.
A sharp crack—the positive-pressure respirator facepiece bursts with a crack; the airtight alarm flashes red.

segments.action: A milky-white Foam Two rolls onto the wet asphalt drill yard, nothing like the wrecked Ladder One.
Supervisor Captain Shi Feng walks onto the yard and talks beside Huo Yan; the two are similar in build.
Shi Feng points at Foam Two, explaining the new response roster to Huo Yan.
Foam Two sounds its horn and leaves; Huo Yan alone on the yard watches it go.
Wind flaps the roster sheet Shi Feng left behind.
From outside the compound comes logistics recruit Xiaowei in an orange-red helmet; at a glance he somewhat resembles young Zhuqing.
Xiaowei practices coiling hose; Huo Yan shakes his head—he is not Zhuqing after all.
Xiaowei leaves the wet asphalt drill yard with an empty hose, back fading down the compound road.
Years later at dusk, Huo Yan with a neck bandage leans on a metal crutch outside the company training hall.
